I imagine this question will come up again, so having something to reference would be good Also <@449019668296892420> -- I think portal will also need to supply more than just the history network, or else how will you service the endpoint `eth_getTransactionByHash`? AFAICT the history network is only able to service blocks, and headers The designs of Portal fundamentally depend on DHT network topology so that you can map data onto specific parts of the network. Each piece of content has a location within the DHT keyspace. This is the mechanism for how data is able to be spread out across the network and still have the data be able to be retrieved. Does this answer the question adequately? Yep thank you -- It seems that portal uses discv5, will this cause any friction/issues with folks that are already familiar with discv4? Doesn't discv4 also have a dht? Whats the advantage of moving to discv5? Discv4 isn't extensible and Discv4 has significant overhead on individual messages since they all have to be signed (if I'm remembering correctly) Are clients looking to move to discv5 in the future? The overhead doesn't seem to be too big of a problem if we seed era1 files I feel like you're suggesting alternate solutions without actually having an understanding of the existing solution... Thats a different solution? Yes might be, thanks for educating me! Also can a client dev (maybe <@360491619402776577> 🙂 ) confirm that post 4444, we want the following rpc methods to work as is (copy pasted from ethereum site): ``` eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber eth_getUncleCountByBlockHash eth_getUncleCountByBlockNumber eth_getBlockByHash eth_getBlockByNumber eth_getTransactionByHash eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex eth_getTransactionReceipt eth_getUncleByBlockHashAndIndex eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex ``` We have solution that I'm pretty sure does what you guys want... and if it doesn't, I'm really interested in understanding where those shortfals are... For full nodes If we moved our eth protocol to discv5, would we need to change something else to distribute the data? I think we first need consensus on what the external API will look like for full nodes post 44444 -- because right now, I think we still want to be able to query a tx by hash We have plans for how to do tx-by-hash. It's easy, it just isn't high priority. Isn't it the Execution Canonical Transaction Index Network? I don't understand this question... Correct, but it's probably very outdated, but at it's core it describes how to do tx-by-hash lookups I'm also trying to get a view on what if anything would need to be done for Portal to be ready, which is why I'm probing so much 😄 I'm generally 👎 on this framing, the idea of being ready.... we are ready... and while there may be additional functionality that we end up wanting, that's a collaborative process among all the clients using and supporting the network. If for example we need `eth_getTransactionByHash` and the `Execution Canonical Transaction Index Network` is the thing that provides that but it is not complete, then I think it would be seen as not ready right? Maybe `complete` is a better phrasing here Ready was referring to it being able to service the needs of 44444 now I don't think that's accurate, aren't clients already ditching old transaction hashes to reduce the local size of this index? Regardless of whether clients are discarding transaction hash lookups.... is your question to understand the roadmap, or to determine whether it makes sense for clients to implement our protocol now or to "wait" until something is more done? I don't know -- this question https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/953349957400821860/1243233313079169025 would clear up what would need to be supported and what would not need to be supported, which in turn would say whether the transaction index network would be needed for 44444 I have no opinion on whether it makes sense to implement now or wait -- its more on what needs to be done for us to say "X has been implemented and it serves all of the needs" We support everything here in our history network except `eth_getTransactionByHash` and `eth_getTransactionReceipt` which require the canonical indices network And I'm pretty sure we can actually implement the canonical indices network faster than a new client can join history network... it's a pretty simple network Ah cool, thanks for the clarification maybe said better, if EL clients show up and are implementing our protoocl and it is clear that tx-by-hash lookups are important, we will prioritize that in our roadmap Links to portal history specs are now pinned in this channel to be easier to find To answer another question in that document I listed, is the workflow you are envisioning this: - Start up EL + Portal Client - EL specifies X MB for the portal network - Portal client will poll the EL for the the latest finalized blocks - Portal client will seed the history network with whatever finalized block the EL gives them - EL will delete blocks that are 1 year old -- these should have been in the portal network for a year by now If we agree that the external API will not change, then the time to delete historical blocks can be client specific We already have infrastructure that is responsible for making sure new blocks get into the network, and that if data goes missing from history that it is re-seeded... So EL implementations *can* choose to do active seeding of data but they don't have to so these two are optional: > - Portal client will poll the EL for the the latest finalized blocks > - Portal client will seed the history network with whatever finalized block the EL gives them I think to move forward, there are two things which are needed: - (Easy) Client devs agree that the methods listed above will not change, wrt their externally observed behaviour after 44444 - Client devs to agree on the path forward to integrating History recovery: - Are client devs okay with plugging in the portal client? - If not, is this due to the perceived complexity of it, or is it mainly the fact that you are delegating networking/historical block retrieval to another entity? - Is seeding the network important for client devs or are you happy with just checking that it exists in the portal network and then deleting blocks? Coming in as portal network noob EL dev, do we expect clients to be able to serve historical txs (in rpc) in the 4444 mvp? Seems like a nice to have but not super critical, more critical from the reth pov would be ability for the portal client to easily fetch tons of old blocks when the user wants to bootstrap an archive node I think in the MVP it likely does not matter, but in the finalized version it would make sense to not change any external behaviour, unless we were going to change that anyways makes sense We have plans and designs to allow bulk retrieval of history... but they are lower priority for us absent someone who actively wants to consume the data that way... so I'd advocate for step-1 being implementation of the history network as-is, and then for bulk retrieval to be an upgrade to the network a bit later once the initial implementations from EL clients are online and working. I wonder if there are any implicit speed requirements here? In that hackmd, it was noted that clients may want to use torrent files for this or a separate archive node network for this purpose (<@226589605816696832>) was working on the EIP I think maybe, as I see it defaults are sticky so archive nodes may also be responsible for seeding on whatever medium is used Our longer term roadmap will include functionality that effectively allows the equivalent of torrenting for large ranges of block history directly from portal, but as I said, this is a lower priority feature absent someone who's ready to consume this data. the impetus driving this development is that today, every execution client must store all block history which takes up hundreds of gb of space, for what is effectively dead data. once you can store blocks somewhere else, you can generate _everything else_ really, so tx and everything else is secondary really Yeah, easy intermediate hack for EL clients to preserve tx-by-hash lookups would be to still retain the local index for the interum until portal can provide it. Yeah this is not on the critical items, so I think its low priority -- It would be good to get numbers on how long it would take to do it with bulk retrieval as we may be able to not need to do the extra items on the list that were intended for fast archive node syncing This means that although a client does not store historical blocks, they will need to maintain a tx hash to block index lookup, to then ask portal network for the block? yes - a client that wants to offer tx lookups can create its own index and still be wildly better off with portal backing it, in terms of disk space usage. I think disk space wise this is true, the full node would need to sync all of the historical blocks from the portal network in this world right? Gonna bump this for client devs, since I think these are the questions halting momentum Lots of options here... They could also pull this from era files for faster bulk creation of the historical index and discard the files after processing the transactions... something to keep in mind is that every consensus client already stores blocks for 6 months - the likely flow here is that consensus will be responsible for 6 months and portal for anything older - an execution client in this world does not need its current eth/ protocol to sync and the requirements for portal to have current data are significantly reduced https://notes.ethereum.org/@rudolf/4444-breakout is a useful background document for anyone that hasn't read it yet This document is confusing as in it will cause a lot of confusion on what portal does/is I think the biggest thing I'm excited about here is EL devs learning about the nuances of how Portal works. There's a massive solution space in DHT networks that we get to take advantage of to solve problems... I'm confident that in the 2-4 year timeline we'll be able to have competitive fully portal based alternatives for: - Bulk historical block syncing - Full syncing of HEAD state - Full archive node state syncing - Out-of-protocol state expiry that still allows fast EVM execution while being able to discard most of the state data We already know how to do all of these things and are simply bottlenecked by how fast we can implement features. There was a lot of discussion around era files, I was hoping to not involve them as that seemed to be pretty contentious as to how to handle them amongst the EL -- If ELs are happy with that then I think its great (I do think we should have some solution in place for this, so that we have a full story of what 44444 will look like in the end) That post had already assumed that EL would store one years worth of blocks, so the six month number seems minor unless I'm missing something <https://hackmd.io/@6iQDuIePQjyYBqDChYw_jg/BkgzJ3EmR> This document made by kev, deme (kim from fluffy/nimbus) audited it and submitted corrections that are in now. I think this is more clear I could probably try to leave comments on what I think is confusing in the first document if that would be beneficial This was also shown to at least someone on each EL team (I think some of the folks who would be dealing with 4444 were not there or there was no-one assigned yet, so I put a star next to their name) the el doesn't need to store any block data - that's perhaps the significant takeaway of my comment .. from 4444, there's also a work item to create a reasonable cl/el sync mechanism so the cl can drive el block histo

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: The designs of Portal fundamentally depend on DHT network topology so that you can map data onto specific parts of the network.  Each piece of content has a location within the DHT keyspace.  This is the mechanism for how data is able to be spread out across the network and still have the data be able to be retrieved.  Does this answer the question adequately?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
To answer another question in that document I listed, is the workflow you are envisioning this:

- Start up EL + Portal Client
- EL specifies X MB for the portal network
- Portal client will poll the EL for the the latest finalized blocks
- Portal client will seed the history network with whatever finalized block the EL gives them
- EL will delete blocks that are 1 year old -- these should have been in the portal network for a year by now

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: If we agree that the external API will not change, then the time to delete historical blocks can be client specific

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
We already have infrastructure that is responsible for making sure new blocks get into the network, and that if data goes missing from history that it is re-seeded...

So EL implementations *can* choose to do active seeding of data but they don't have to so these two are optional:

> - Portal client will poll the EL for the the latest finalized blocks
> - Portal client will seed the history network with whatever finalized block the EL gives them

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I think to move forward, there are two things which are needed:

- (Easy) Client devs agree that the methods listed above will not change, wrt their externally observed behaviour after 44444

- Client devs to agree on the path forward to integrating History recovery:
     - Are client devs okay with plugging in the portal client?
     - If not, is this due to the perceived complexity of it, or is it mainly the fact that you are delegating networking/historical block retrieval to another entity?
- Is seeding the network important for client devs or are you happy with just checking that it exists in the portal network and then deleting blocks?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
I think the biggest thing I'm excited about here is EL devs learning about the nuances of how Portal works.  There's a massive solution space in DHT networks that we get to take advantage of to solve problems...  I'm confident that in the 2-4 year timeline we'll be able to have competitive fully portal based alternatives for:

- Bulk historical block syncing
- Full syncing of HEAD state
- Full archive node state syncing
- Out-of-protocol state expiry that still allows fast EVM execution while being able to discard most of the state data

We already know how to do all of these things and are simply bottlenecked by how fast we can implement features.

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content:
yeah, I need a developer with free time - other than that, it's on the roadmap already - so .. both of the documents have some confusion and some gems in them - I'd look at both as sort of "user stories" that need to be distilled into actionable items. 

this is actually all a lot more simple than it seems, from a client POV: today, there exists a devp2p protocol (eth/6x) for syncing execution client - if an EL implements that protocol fetching the data from portal instead of its own local block store, that node will be indistinguishable from one storing the blocks locally (assuming portal serves the blocks) -> there's an upgrade path in which the users don't even notice this work has been done (specially if they're running validators / consensus clients and not much else)

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: I can say this _because_ there exist multiple layers of backups for the above strategy: era files, archive nodes, current full nodes that can cover our asses while the feature stabilises and so on - these are all good things that have happened in the past year or so, which is why now is a good time for 4444 (finally)
